_comment: Hindu expansion 175-drive K: Vishnu Purana narratives (Wilson 1840, public domain).

texts.period: Vishnu Purana, Book I, chs. 12-13, c. 300-800 CE (Wilson translation, 1840)

source.work: The Vishnu Purana, trans. H. H. Wilson (1840), Book I, the story of Dhruva

summary.en: Five-year-old Dhruva climbed his father's knee and was pushed off by his stepmother: no seat for the son of a rival wife, and none but the king's own. His mother's advice - seek the one whose seat never shakes - sent the boy into the forest; he stood on one leg in tapas until Vishnu came, touched his cheek, and set him above the turning sky: the pole star is a child who was denied a lap.
summary.zh: 五歲的達魯婆爬上父親之膝，被繼母推下：妃嬪之子的座位不屬於他，唯有王座除外。母親的忠告——去找那位座位永不動搖者——將男孩送入森林；他一足而立行苦行，直到毘濕奴前來，觸其面頰，將他安置於旋轉的天空之上：北極星即那位未被允許坐膝的孩童。

sensitivity.note: Living tradition (Dhruva recited in devotional instruction); classified 'myth'.

passages.text: The boy climbed the king's knee as kings' sons do, and the senior queen pulled him off with the sentence that made a saint of him: only my son sits the lap; go to thy mother, and ask her for a seat elsewhere.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Vishnu Purana, Book I (Wilson 1840); not verbatim.

passages.text: His mother told him plainly: she had no seat to give but the one that cannot be given by a king - seek the Lord whose seat never falls; and the boy walked into the forest at five. The tapas is a child's enormity: one leg, breath stopped, the forest burning around a fixed point - until Vishnu's hand came down and offered him a seat in the sky's own pivot, the star that does not set.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Vishnu Purana, Book I (Wilson 1840); not verbatim.

region.zh: 薩拉斯瓦蒂平原（象徵性定位）

texts.period: Vishnu Purana, Book I, ch. 13, c. 300-800 CE (Wilson translation, 1840)

source.work: The Vishnu Purana, trans. H. H. Wilson (1840), Book I, Prithu and the Earth

summary.en: When a wicked king starved the earth, the seers churned the dead king's arm and produced Prithu, the first consecrated king - and the earth, made woman, fled from his bow like a cow from the brand. She consented to be milked instead: Prithu levelled her fields, and from her every creature then milked its own food - the first agriculture, and the charter of kingship as a covenant, not a conquest.
summary.zh: 惡王使大地饑饉之際，仙人們攪動亡王之臂而生出缽哩陀——首位受冕之王——而化為女子的大地如母牛見烙印般逃避其弓。她轉而允許被擠乳：缽哩陀平整其田，自此萬物皆自她擠得各自之食——最早的農耕，以及王權作為盟約而非征服的憲章。

passages.text: The kingless earth grew wild and thin; from the right arm of the slain tyrant the seers kneaded out Prithu, and the rites made him the first of consecrated kings. The Earth fled him in a woman's shape, and he chased her with a bow across the worlds until she stopped - 'slay me and who will feed thy subjects?' - and offered the cow's bargain instead.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Vishnu Purana, Book I (Wilson 1840); not verbatim.

passages.text: So the king levelled her fields and became her herdsman: every creature milked its own food from her - herbs to the brahmin, grain to the merchant, grass to the deer - and kingship was defined as the keeping of a covenant with the ground.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Vishnu Purana, Book I (Wilson 1840); not verbatim.

texts.period: Vishnu Purana, Book V, c. 300-800 CE (Wilson translation, 1840)

source.work: The Vishnu Purana, trans. H. H. Wilson (1840), Book V, Putana

summary.en: Kamsa sent a shape-changing demoness to nurse the infants of Vraja - she was beautiful, and her breast was poison. The baby Krishna drank, and the drink was fatal to the nurse: she grew to her true giantess size, blackened the landscape with her fall, and the poison she meant for the child was counted by the village as his first miracle.
summary.zh: 甘薩遣一變形羅剎女為牧區之嬰兒授乳——她貌美，其乳即毒。嬰孩克里希那飲之，而毒反噬其乳母：她現出真身巨妖之形，墜落之體黑遍大地；村人將那本欲毒死嬰兒的毒計數為他的第一件奇蹟。

passages.text: The demoness walked into the herdsmen's village as a lovely stranger, offering to nurse the most darling baby of the season - the one born at midnight to Nanda's house. The child drank what was meant to kill him, and held on: the nurse's body swelled to her true size, a giantess blackening the horizon as she fell - the poison drawn into the poisoner. The village counted its miracle and its funeral in one breath; Yashoda found her baby laughing in the dust - the first proof, in the village's eyes, of what the mother did not yet know she had adopted.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Vishnu Purana, Book V (Wilson 1840); not verbatim.

title.zh: 克里希那舞於迦利耶百首之上

region.zh: 迦林蒂河亞穆納段（象徵性定位）

texts.period: Vishnu Purana, Book V, c. 300-800 CE (Wilson translation, 1840)

source.work: The Vishnu Purana, trans. H. H. Wilson (1840), Book V, Kaliya

summary.en: The hundred-headed serpent Kaliya poisoned the Yamuna: birds fell from the branches, the water smoked. Krishna leapt from a kadamba tree into the pool and danced - on the serpent's heads, each coil pinned under a child's foot, until the great snake's wives rose from the water to beg for his life. Krishna spared him on one condition: go, and never come back to my river.
summary.zh: 百首蛇王迦利耶毒化了亞穆納河：禽鳥自枝頭墜落，水面冒煙。克里希那自瞻蔔樹躍入池中，在蛇王之首上舞蹈——每一盤曲都被孩童之足釘住——直到巨蛇的妻妾自水中升起為其求命。克里希那以一條件饒之：去吧，永不回到我的河中。

passages.text: The river had become a poison: cattle refused its banks, birds fell into the water unburned by any fire, and the village learned which pool to fear. Krishna dived in without armor and came up in the coils - then stood, and danced, a child's bare feet keeping time on a hundred heads until the serpent's strength was the tune's. The wives' pleading saved the dancer's prisoner: he was sent to the far sea with his lives intact - the dance's mercy as famous as the dance's stamping; the Yamuna ran sweet from that hour.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Vishnu Purana, Book V (Wilson 1840); not verbatim.

title.en: Krishna Kills Kamsa in the Arena
title.zh: 克里希那於鬥技場誅甘薩

region.zh: 馬圖拉鬥技場（象徵性定位）

texts.period: Vishnu Purana, Book V, c. 300-800 CE (Wilson translation, 1840)

source.work: The Vishnu Purana, trans. H. H. Wilson (1840), Book V, Kamsa's death

summary.en: Invited to Mathura for a festival and a wrestling match, Krishna walked into the arena where the tyrant had raised the bow of Shiva as bait. He bent and broke the bow; the wrestlers Chanura and Mushtika were sent at the cowherd boys and were broken instead; and Krishna, seizing his uncle by the hair on the dais itself, ended the prophecy in front of the whole city - the child of the massacre decree killing the man who wrote it.
summary.zh: 受邀赴馬圖拉慶典與角力賽的克里希那，走入暴君以濕婆神弓為餌設下的鬥技場。他彎折並折斷神弓；奉命對付牧童的摔角手迦奴羅與穆什底迦反被折斷；克里希那在高臺上抓住舅舅的頭髮，當著全城終結預言——屠嬰令所針對的孩子親手誅殺了下令者。

passages.text: The arena was a trap with decoration: the bow of Shiva set in the center to be admired - and the herdsman boy bent it with one hand, and broke it with the sound of an omen. Chanura, the champion, was assigned the child by the king's smile; the wrestler went into the dust and did not leave it - the cowherd's arms were his father the Wind's. The prophecy's author died at the hands of its subject: Krishna took his uncle by the hair where the whole city could watch, and the tyrant who had counted his wife's children found his own counted at last.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Vishnu Purana, Book V (Wilson 1840); not verbatim.

region.zh: 恭提那與維陀爾薄（象徵性定位）

texts.period: Vishnu Purana, Book V, c. 300-800 CE (Wilson translation, 1840)

source.work: The Vishnu Purana, trans. H. H. Wilson (1840), Book V, Rukmini

summary.en: Rukmini, princess of Vidarbha, loved Krishna and was promised to Shishupala; the day before the wedding she sent him a letter with her plan: come at dawn with a chariot and take me from the temple before the bridegroom's procession arrives. Krishna came, lifted her into the chariot in front of the assembled kings - and fought his way out against the wedding armies.
summary.zh: 維陀爾薄公主魯克彌尼愛克里希那，卻被許給尸市場沙巴拉；婚禮前一日，她送信告知計劃：拂曉攜車而來，於迎親行列到達前從神廟將我帶走。克里希那到來，當著會集諸王將她抱上戰車——並衝破送親軍陣殺出。

passages.text: The letter was her own elopement-plan written in full: come before the wedding sun, take me at the temple, and let no king's procession finish its arrival - a bride engineering her own abduction. He came at dawn, swept her up from the shrine where she was said to be praying to the rival bridegroom's patron, and the wedding's shock troops found an empty temple and a chariot already past the gates. The running battle that followed cleared the road behind the flying chariot - and the marriage it produced became the model of Krishna's queenship in Dvaraka; the letter is the tradition's first love-letter with tactics.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Vishnu Purana, Book V (Wilson 1840); not verbatim.

title.en: The Curse at Dvaraka: The Yadavas' Last Feast
title.zh: 達瓦迦之咒：耶度族的最後宴席

region.zh: 般羅婆沙海岸聖地（象徵性定位）

texts.period: Vishnu Purana, Book V, chs. 35-38; Mausala tradition, c. 300-800 CE (Wilson translation, 1840)

source.work: The Vishnu Purana, trans. H. H. Wilson (1840), Book V, the end of the Yadavas

summary.en: At a pilgrimage-feast the Yadavas drank, quarreled, and turned their hands to grass that became iron reeds, slaughtering each other to the last man on the beach - the fulfillment of a seer's curse and Gandhari's. Krishna sat apart under a tree; a hunter's arrow took him for a sleeping deer and struck the one mortal spot - the sole unarmored place the Lord had left himself.
summary.zh: 朝聖宴上，耶度族人飲酒、口角、以手握草化為鐵蘆而互相屠殺，於海灘上戰至最後一人——應驗仙人之咒與甘陀利之詛。克里希那獨坐樹下；獵人之箭誤其為睡鹿，射中主為自己留下的唯一不設防之處。

passages.text: The seer's curse had named the instruments: grass shall be your iron. The drunk warriors pulled reeds from the ground and found each one a blade - and the beach at Prabhasa did the arithmetic. By evening the race of Yadu was a field of the fallen; Krishna walked the shore of his own people's ruin, and the women of Dvaraka began the wailing that Gandhari had promised them.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Vishnu Purana, Book V (Wilson 1840); not verbatim.

passages.text: The hunter's arrow found the heel-mark of the god's own choice: the Lord of the universe kept one mortal spot for himself, and left the world there - the sky filled with the leaving, and the age of heroes ended on a beach.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Vishnu Purana, Book V (Wilson 1840); not verbatim.

title.en: Garuda and the Amrita of the Gods

region.en: Cosmic ocean and Indra's heaven (symbolic pin)
region.zh: 宇宙之海與因陀羅天界（象徵性定位）

texts.period: Vishnu Purana, Book I, chs. 29-31, c. 300-800 CE (Wilson translation, 1840)

source.work: The Vishnu Purana, trans. H. H. Wilson (1840), Book I, Garuda and the amrita

summary.en: The Purana's Garuda version is a covenant-story: sent to steal the amrita as his mother's ransom, the great bird quenched a forest-fire by drinking a river, outwitted the gods' guards, took the nectar in his claws - and Vishnu appeared, not to fight but to bargain: the bird shall be immortal without drinking, and the god's own carrier forever. Indra's thunderbolt was returned with the ransom paid and the amrita taken back.
summary.zh: 往世書的金翅鳥版本是一則盟約故事：為贖其母而奉命竊取甘露，巨鳥飲盡一條河以撲滅森林之火，以智勝過諸神的守衛，以爪取走神露——毘濕奴現身，非為交戰而為交易：鳥不飲而得不死，並成為神之座騎直到永遠。因陀羅的雷霆杵隨贖金之付與神露之取回而物歸原主。

passages.text: The ransom the serpents demanded was the one thing the gods hoarded: the amrita - and Garuda's wings measured the distance between a mother's slavery and heaven's strong-room. The obstacles fell to scale and wit: a forest-fire quenched with a river swallowed, the guards of the nectar outflown - and the great bird left the theft without drinking a drop. Vishnu's offer changed the story's species: immortality without the theft, wings under the god forever - the bird kept his bargain and Indra's bolt retrieved the jar; the ransom was paid in honor rather than in nectar.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Vishnu Purana, Book I (Wilson 1840); not verbatim.

title.en: Prahlada in the Furnace of His Father's Anger
title.zh: 布羅赫拉達於父怒之火爐中

region.zh: 金輪王之都（象徵性定位）

texts.period: Vishnu Purana, Book I, chs. 15-17, c. 300-800 CE (Wilson translation, 1840)

source.work: The Vishnu Purana, trans. H. H. Wilson (1840), Book I, the persecution of Prahlada

summary.en: The persecution chapters of the Narasimha cycle are a catalogue of failed murders: poison that the boy blessed, fire that cooled around him, elephants that knelt, the fall from a palace balcony caught by the earth. Prahlada's defense in every scene was a sentence his father could not counter - He is in me as He is in the pillar - and each failure made the boy's theology more public.
summary.zh: 獅面人循環中的迫害章節是一份失敗謀殺的目錄：被孩童祝禱的毒、圍繞他轉涼的火、跪下的巨象、被大地接住的宮殿墜落。布羅赫拉達在每一幕中的辯護都是一句父親無法反駁的話——祂在我中，如祂在柱中——而每一次失敗都使孩童的神學更為公開。

passages.text: The poison was served in the boy's own cup and blessed before drinking; the fire was built to burn him and cooled around the one child inside it; the elephant that was to trample him knelt. The balcony, the ocean, the serpents: the catalogue of a father's methods - and the son's reply never varied: He is in the pillar as He is in me; the whole world is His pillar. Each public failure made the theology public: the boy who would not die for saying Vishnu's name became the court's teacher, and the father's rage had nowhere left to hide from the sentence its own child kept repeating.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Vishnu Purana, Book I (Wilson 1840); not verbatim.
